episodes.title: Turning Makeup into an Enterprise: Vocational Education & Brand Building
episodes.summary: Wengelawit (Liya) Gole, founder and CEO of International Makeup School (IMS) and Dura by Liya, joins Meri Podcast to share how she transitioned from corporate accounting and aviation to pioneering professional vocational beauty education in Ethiopia. She details overcoming early societal skepticism, professionalizing makeup artistry as an accredited career, navigating high import tariffs on cosmetics, and scaling multi-branch service and retail operations.

guest.name: Wengelawit (Liya) Gole
guest.title: Founder & CEO
guest.company: International Makeup School & Liya Gole Beauty
guest.bio: Ethiopian beauty entrepreneur, educator, and founder of International Makeup School (IMS), Liya Gole Salon, and Dura by Liya. Formerly an accounting and private aviation employee, she established Ethiopia's first accredited vocational makeup institute, training thousands of certified beauty professionals across the nation.

insights.title: Legitimizing Informal Trades Through Structured Accreditation
insights.summary: Transforming a dismissed service craft into a respected commercial enterprise requires formalizing curriculum, securing institutional accreditation, and setting professional service benchmarks.
takeaways: Societal skepticism ('who goes to school to learn makeup?') was overcome by establishing rigorous vocational standards rather than informal apprenticeships.
Formal certification transformed personal creative talent into an institutional business that trained over 1,200 Ethiopian professionals and 2,600 overall.
Initial market demand was validated organically when over 1,300 students registered for IMS before launch without celebrity endorsements or mass media campaigns.
insights.practicalAction: Standardize service protocols into a documented training curriculum before attempting to expand branch locations or recruit staff.

insights.title: Disciplined Capital Reinvestment Over Passive Extraction
insights.summary: Service enterprises achieve operational durability when leadership constantly separates mere busywork from productive execution and reinvests cash flows back into capacity.
takeaways: Continuously audit organizational energy by asking: 'Are we genuinely being productive, or merely keeping ourselves busy?'
Work is not an entity that takes capital and stays silent; dedicated operational reinvestment reliably yields compounding institutional returns.
Frontier market hurdles—from 300% luxury import tariffs to regulatory delays—cannot be solved by foreign textbooks; persistent, iterative trial is mandatory.
insights.practicalAction: Conduct regular leadership check-ins evaluating whether daily operational tasks directly expand enterprise productivity or simply generate routine noise.

quotations.amharicQuote: ቢዚ ነሽ ወይስ ፕሮዳክቲቭ ነሽ ነው ሁል ጊዜ እራሴን ምጠይቀው ነገር ማለት ነው።
quotations.englishTranslation: Are you busy or are you productive? That is what I always ask myself.
quotations.speaker: Wengelawit (Liya) Gole
quotations.context: Reflecting on executive time allocation while balancing school administration, salon operations, and accessories retail.

quotations.amharicQuote: ስራ ሰው አይደለም ብር ወስዶ ፀጥ አይልም፤ ስራ ስትሰጠው ይሰጣል።
quotations.englishTranslation: Work is not like a person who takes money and stays silent; when you invest in work, work gives back.
quotations.speaker: Wengelawit (Liya) Gole
quotations.context: Explaining the compounding returns of reinvesting operational effort and capital into International Makeup School.

quotations.amharicQuote: ስታርት ካልጀመርክ የትም አትደርስም። እዚህ ሀገር የሚገጥሙ ነገሮች ቢዝነስ ቡክ ውስጥ የሉም፤ ሞክር እምቢ ካለህ ሞክር ነው።
quotations.englishTranslation: If you don't start, you won't get anywhere. The challenges you face in this country are not in business books; you try, and if it resists, you try again.
quotations.speaker: Wengelawit (Liya) Gole
quotations.context: Addressing aspiring Ethiopian entrepreneurs on navigating operational friction and systemic market hurdles.
